prose: In this Dutch-language piece ('Don't break yourself on your own government'), Bert Hubert argues that the Dutch government has written rules for its own use of cloud, AI and other algorithms - and almost never follows them. The Algemene Rekenkamer, the national audit office, found that for two-thirds of government cloud IT projects the mandatory risk assessment was not merely inadequate but entirely absent. A report by ABDTOPconsult, an internal investigation body, adds that recent tests of the obligatory fallback plans all failed.

Hubert also raises the unresolved legal question of whether GDPR article 9 special-category personal data - including health data - may be stored in American clouds at all. Government-commissioned research indicates this is permitted only with an extra protective encryption layer, a requirement everyone quietly ignores because it is too difficult. His warning: citizens should not let their own government's habitual non-compliance become their problem.
highlights: Dutch original: 'Ga niet kapot aan je eigen overheid'
The Dutch government sets rules for cloud, AI and algorithms - then ignores them
Audit office: two-thirds of government cloud projects had no mandatory risk assessment at all
ABDTOPconsult: every test of the required fallback plans failed
Open question: may GDPR article 9 data (incl. health data) go to US clouds at all?
Government's own research: only with extra encryption - which everyone skips as too hard
